lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Gerald, Jean here. How's your Monday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi! Yes, now's good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I'm doing the best I can.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Dinner's late at your house.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, the late dinners makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat dinner at the same time every day?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the late dinners keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're really honest with yourself, and that helps.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to walk after every dinner. That's the meal that matters most for your sugar.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. Between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 6. Maybe 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, if it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, so your plan this week is to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days. Did I get that right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Gerald, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

flags.reason: Warning that health will suffer, pushed without permission; undermines autonomy and partnership.
Repeats the walk suggestion verbatim after the participant already responded; ignores the prior answer.
'You have to walk after every dinner' is a directive that contradicts the stated autonomy.
'You have to make this a priority' pushes after the participant voiced ability at line 37; missed change talk.

score.summary: Jean used good reflections and open questions in the middle of the call, which helped Gerald name barriers and commit to three 10-minute walks. However, she repeatedly directed him ('You have to...', 'If you don't do this...') and repeated the same suggestion verbatim, which undercut the autonomy she claimed to offer.
strengths: Line 13 and 21: complex reflections captured Gerald's ambivalence about late dinners.
Line 15 and 49: open questions explored his reasons and anticipated barriers.
Line 51: clear summary of the agreed plan with a check for accuracy, followed by a next contact at line 53.
coaching_tips: Line 8, 36, 38: replace 'You have to' and warnings with reflections or permission-based advice, e.g., 'Would it help to talk through what a walk could look like?'
Line 29: do not repeat advice verbatim; after line 28 'Sure', respond to what Gerald said about planning the night before (line 30).
Line 37: respond to Gerald's confidence ('I know I can do it, I did it before') with a reflection or affirmation rather than a directive, and build on it.
Line 3 and 27: vary your approach and avoid repeating the same permission script; ask only once before offering information.
